status: DRAFT v0 - requires PO sign-off before it is used as the S2 redaction rule-set (US-7, FR-2.4)
regex_dialect: Python 3 `re` (compile with re.IGNORECASE only where `flags` says so). Patterns are candidate generators, not the final decision: every hit is scored with checksum/context/NER before the action is applied.

T1.name: Restricted
T1.definition: National identification numbers (NRIC/FIN/passport and similar) and any data prescribed in the Schedule (Part 1) or reg 3(1)(b) of the PDP (Notification of Data Breaches) Regulations 2021, where a breach is deemed to cause significant harm when combined with name or ID number. Also policy-restricted categories (minors, credentials).
T1.handling: Never leaves the tenant in clear. Any remaining T1 pattern candidate blocks egress; checksum failure cannot clear it. Highest audit sensitivity.

T2.name: Sensitive
T2.definition: Direct contact/location identifiers and quasi-identifiers (personal phone, personal email, residential address, date of birth, vehicle number, account/customer ids, special attributes by policy).
T2.handling: Never leaves the tenant in clear. High-confidence residual hits block; medium-confidence candidates are redacted or resolved by review before egress.

T3.name: Personal
T3.definition: Other personal data: names, business contact information, online identifiers.
T3.handling: Pseudonymised before egress. Egress guard blocks on high-confidence hits not covered by a placeholder.

C.name: Client-confidential (not personal data)
C.definition: Identifiers of client and counterparty organisations (names, UEN), firm file references. Not personal data under PDPA s 2 unless they identify an individual (e.g. a sole proprietor), but confidential under Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules 2015 r 6 and Evidence Act ss 128/128A.
C.handling: Pseudonymised before egress by default (FR-2.4). Firm policy may relax for counterparty names only (open PO question Q-7).

actions.PSEUDONYMISE: Replace the span with a stable typed placeholder (see `placeholder`). Store original-to-placeholder mapping in the tenant redaction map. Model outputs containing the placeholder are re-identified inside the tenant when rendered for a user with matter access.
actions.MASK: Replace the span with a typed placeholder. The mapping is NOT used to re-insert the value into AI-generated text: outputs keep the placeholder and the UI shows 'value withheld - see source document'. The original remains only in the original document store.
actions.DROP: Remove the span or object from the model payload entirely and insert a neutral marker [OMITTED_<TYPE>]. No mapping is stored. Used for credentials/secrets and for images (signatures, photos, ID scans), which are never sent to an external model.
actions.BLOCK: Do not send the excerpt to any external model. Flag for lawyer handling and audit the refusal. A firm-policy override cannot authorise unredacted external egress: that requires an explicit recorded PO exception under AGENTS.md, plus the responsible lawyer's matter approval and other release controls. Neither approval is implied by this taxonomy.
actions.KEEP: Not redacted (e.g. public bodies, statutes, courts, arbitral institutions). Listed so that the egress guard does not treat it as a miss.

placeholder.numbering: n starts at 1 per TYPE, in order of first appearance in the matter.
placeholder.stability: The same normalised value receives the same placeholder for every model call in the same matter. Different matters never share placeholders (prevents cross-matter linkage).

normalisation.PERSON: alias cluster: full name, surname with honorific, given name, initials resolved by coreference; lawyer can merge/split clusters in the redaction review UI
normalisation.ORG: legal name with and without suffix (Pte. Ltd., Pte Ltd, Ltd, LLP) and defined short names are one cluster

placeholder.collision_rule: If the source text already contains a string matching `placeholder.regex`, escape it (e.g. replace '[' with '\u27e6' in the payload) before redaction and restore after re-identification, so source text can never be confused with a Verina placeholder.
placeholder.type_label_leakage: Placeholders reveal only the category (e.g. that an NRIC exists), never any character of the value.

reidentification.mapping_store_location: Tenant database in the Singapore region (DATA_FLOW.md F5, 'Redaction map'), encrypted with the tenant data key; crypto-shredded on matter deletion.
never: sent to any model provider or other external service
written to application logs, telemetry or error reports
included in metadata-only audit records (prompt/output copies require a separately reviewed encrypted evidence store)
accessible to Verina staff without a customer-approved, time-boxed, audited support grant
reidentification.when: At render or export time, for a user who passes the matter ACL and ethical-wall check (NFR-4).
reidentification.legal_note: Pseudonymised data is still personal data while the mapping exists (PDPA s 2 'personal data' limb (b); PDPC Guide to Basic Anonymisation: de-identification is only the first step of anonymisation). Unauthorised re-identification of anonymised information by an individual can be an offence (PDPA s 48F).

detection_pipeline.locality: All detection runs inside the tenant boundary. No external API (including the model provider) may be used to detect PII, because that would itself be an unredacted egress.
stages: 1. Intake dictionary: parties, client and counterparty names, signatories and contacts captured at intake (FR-1.1) seed exact/alias matches.
2. Pattern + checksum layer: regex candidates from `categories[].detection.regex`, validated by checksum where defined (NRIC/FIN, Luhn).
3. Context layer: keyword windows (default 40 characters either side) raise or lower confidence.
4. Local NER model: PERSON, ORG, ADDRESS/LOC, DATE; plus a local lexicon for health and other T1 special categories.
5. Coreference/alias resolution so that 'Tan Ah Kow', 'Mr Tan' and 'Ah Kow' share one placeholder.
6. Lawyer review: placeholder list shown before the first model call on a matter (US-7); user can add/remove spans; changes are audit-logged.
7. Egress guard (independent second detector) re-scans the final serialised request; fails closed (DATA_FLOW.md section 4).

confidence_bands.high: >= 0.85: action applied automatically; guard blocks if found unredacted.
confidence_bands.medium: 0.50-0.85: action applied automatically (bias to over-redact); surfaced for lawyer review.
confidence_bands.low: < 0.50: not redacted automatically; surfaced as a suggestion only.

detection_pipeline.bias: Over-redaction is preferred to under-redaction. A checksum failure LOWERS confidence but never by itself prevents redaction of an NRIC-shaped string (typos and synthetic numbers are common).

acceptance_targets_proposed.measured_on: Synthetic SG PII test set (Gate 1, Sprint 2). Targets are proposals pending PO approval (Q-5).

nric_fin_checksum.note: ICA does not publish the checksum algorithm. This is the widely documented community algorithm. It reproduces the NRIC examples we checked, but the M-series letter table is unconfirmed: ICA's illustrative example 'M1234567B' does not validate under it. Use for confidence scoring only.
nric_fin_checksum.procedure: sum(digit_i * weight_i) + prefix_offset[prefix]; r = sum mod 11; expected_letter = check_letter_tables[prefix][r]

luhn.note: Luhn mod 10 is a proposed checksum confidence signal. No ISO primary standard was retrieved in this review. A failed checksum must not by itself allow a contextual card-number candidate through.

categories.label: Individual's name (incl. aliases, initials, honorific forms)
categories.tier_elevation: T1 if the individual is a minor or is linked to any T1 special category in the same matter.

detection.notes: Malay patronymics (bin/binte), Indian (s/o, d/o, a/l, a/p) and Chinese name orders must be handled. Business contact information (PDPA s 4(5)) is still pseudonymised for confidentiality.

categories.false_positive_notes: Defined terms in capitals (e.g. 'the Supplier'), case names in citations (keep: needed for the Verification Ledger), statute names.
pdpa_refs: DBN Regs reg 3(1)(a) (full name + prescribed data)

categories.label: NRIC / FIN number (S, T, F, G, M series), incl. partial or masked forms

detection.notes: Pattern hit alone = medium confidence; pattern + valid checksum or context keyword = high. Partial NRIC (last 3 digits + letter) is still personal data where identifiable (AG NRIC para 5.3).

categories.synthetic_example_warning: Any well-formed NRIC/FIN may belong to a real person. Use only in synthetic fixtures with fictional names; never combine with real names or addresses.
categories.false_positive_notes: Product codes, invoice numbers with the same shape. Context and checksum reduce confidence; over-redaction is acceptable.
pdpa_refs: DBN Regs reg 2 'identification number' and reg 3(1)(a)

categories.label: Other Singapore identity numbers: Birth Certificate number, Work Permit number, other pass numbers

detection.notes: Formats are to verify. AG NRIC para 1.4 extends NRIC treatment to Birth Certificate, FIN and Work Permit numbers. Detection is context-led because the formats overlap with other numbers.

categories.label: Passport number (Singapore and foreign)

detection.notes: SG passport format ([E|K] + 7 digits + letter) is to verify. Foreign passports are detected by context only.

pdpa_refs: AG NRIC para 1.5 (accord passports similar treatment)
DBN Regs reg 2 'identification number' includes passport number

categories.label: Foreign national ID numbers (e.g. Malaysian MyKad, other government-issued IDs)

detection.notes: Format of MyKad (YYMMDD-PB-###G) is to verify. DBN Regs reg 2 'identification number' includes foreign identification numbers.

categories.label: Telephone / mobile number (incl. +65 formats)
categories.personal_data_note: Personal data when it relates to an identifiable individual; a business number is business contact information (s 4(5)) but is still pseudonymised.

detection.notes: SG numbers: 8 digits starting with 3 (VoIP), 6 (fixed line), 8 or 9 (mobile) - to verify against IMDA numbering plan. Bare 8-digit hits without context are medium confidence.

categories.false_positive_notes: Amounts, clause numbers, dates in numeric form. Require separators or context for bare 8-digit hits.

categories.label: Email address
categories.personal_data_note: Personal data if it identifies an individual (e.g. name.surname@...). Generic role mailboxes (legal@, info@) are not personal data but are still pseudonymised when they reveal the client organisation.
categories.tier_note: T3 when it is clearly business contact information.

categories.label: Residential or postal address incl. Singapore postal code, block/unit numbers
categories.personal_data_note: A residential address of an individual is personal data. A registered office address is business information but is pseudonymised with the organisation as client-confidential (tier C).

detection.postal_code_rule: 6 digits. First two digits are the postal sector (01-82 assumed; to verify against SingPost). Bare 6-digit numbers are only treated as postal codes with address context.
detection.notes: Redact the whole address span (street + unit + postal code) as one placeholder. Country and city names alone are KEEP.

categories.label: Bank or finance company account number (incl. IBAN)
categories.personal_data_note: Personal data when the account is an individual's. Company accounts are client-confidential.

detection.notes: SG bank account formats vary by bank (typically 9-12 digits, often hyphenated); context is required. SWIFT/BIC codes and bank names are KEEP (institution identifiers).

categories.label: Credit, charge or debit card number

detection.notes: 13-19 digits with optional separators; Luhn-valid = high confidence. A card number has no legitimate role in contract analysis output, so it is masked and never re-inserted.

categories.synthetic_example_note: These are public payment-network test numbers.

categories.label: Date of birth / age
categories.tier_elevation: T1 if the computed age at document date is under 18 (see minor_flag).

detection.notes: Only dates with DOB context are redacted. Contract dates (effective date, term, notice periods) are KEEP: they are essential to the review.

categories.label: Data relating to a child or young person (under 18)

detection.derived_rule: Any person cluster whose DOB gives age < 18 at the document date, or who is described with minor-context keywords, is tagged MINOR; all of that person's identifiers are elevated to T1 and the matter is flagged.

categories.notes: Personal data identifying a child or young person in CYPA contexts (investigation, arrest, care, court order, proceedings) is prescribed in the DBN Regs Schedule Part 1 item 5 and is handled under special_category_prescribed (BLOCK).
pdpa_refs: DBN Regs Schedule Part 1 item 5 and Part 2 para 3 ('child or young person' = below 18)

categories.label: Health, medical, insurance-claim health information

detection.lexicon_ref: Local medical-term lexicon (diagnoses, conditions, treatments, medications), maintained by PDPA counsel + AI engineer in S2.
detection.notes: Replace the specific health detail, keep a neutral category placeholder so the model can still reason about the clause (e.g. 'the employee's [HEALTH_INFO_1]'). Items in DBN Regs Schedule Part 1 items 18-20 (STDs, HIV, schizophrenia, substance abuse, fertility, abortion, organ donation) go to special_category_prescribed (BLOCK).

synthetic_examples: on medical leave for a back injury

categories.label: Prescribed highly sensitive data: CYPA/VAA matters, sexual-offence victims and witnesses, Women's Charter place of safety, specified medical conditions (items 18-20), suicide or attempted suicide, domestic/child/sexual abuse, adoption

detection.notes: The commercial-contract wedge rarely contains these. Detection triggers BLOCK of the excerpt, a matter flag and lawyer handling. Identification of sexual-offence victims can also be restricted by other written law (to verify per matter).

synthetic_examples: the minor was placed in a place of safety

categories.label: An individual's financial information: remuneration, income, net worth, debts, loans, creditworthiness, investments, insurance policy terms

detection.notes: Only amounts tied to an identifiable individual are redacted. Corporate deal values, fees, liability caps and prices are KEEP by default (they drive the risk review); see PO question Q-8.

categories.label: Passwords, PINs, security answers, API keys, private keys, account credentials

detection.notes: Also run a high-entropy string detector. Secrets are never needed for contract analysis.

pdpa_refs: DBN Regs reg 3(1)(b) (account identifier + access credential)
DBN Regs Schedule Part 1 item 7 (private keys)

categories.label: Handwritten signatures, initials, signature images

detection.notes: Images embedded in DOCX/PDF are never included in model payloads. Typed '/s/ Name' signatures are handled as person_name. The original document keeps the signature (FR-2.1 originals unchanged).

categories.label: Photographs of individuals, ID card scans, biometric data (fingerprints, facial templates)

detection.notes: No image is sent to an external model in MVP. OCR runs locally (DATA_FLOW.md section 5.2) and OCR text goes through the text rules. NRIC card scans: the physical NRIC contains name, photo, thumbprint and address (AG NRIC para 1.3).

pdpa_refs: DBN Regs reg 3(1)(b)(ii) (biometric data used for account access)

categories.label: Vehicle registration number

detection.notes: SG plate format is to verify; context improves precision.

categories.label: Individual's account/customer/employee/policy/CPF/tax reference numbers

detection.notes: CPF account numbers and IRAS tax reference numbers for individuals are typically the NRIC/FIN; they are caught by nric_fin as well.

categories.label: IP addresses, device ids, personal social-media handles/URLs

detection.notes: Mostly relevant to email intake headers (F1e) and logs; in contracts, rare.

categories.label: Race, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, political views, criminal record of an adult (policy category)

detection.notes: Not a statutory 'special category' under the PDPA (the PDPA has none); treated as sensitive by Verina policy because of harm potential. Arrest of a child is prescribed (item 5) and handled by special_category_prescribed.

synthetic_examples: a member of the Example Faith congregation
pdpa_refs: PDPA s 24 (security proportional to sensitivity: AG Key Concepts para 17.2-17.3)

categories.label: Client organisation name (legal name, trading name, defined short name)
categories.personal_data_note: Not personal data, unless the client is a sole proprietor/individual (then also person_name).

detection.notes: Client identity comes from the intake record (FR-1.1). Role assignment (client vs counterparty vs other) uses the intake record; unknown ORGs default to ORG_OTHER handling.

pdpa_refs: Not PDPA; confidentiality: Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules 2015 r 6; Evidence Act 1893 ss 128, 128A; FR-2.4

categories.label: Counterparty organisation name

detection.notes: Firm AI policy may allow counterparty names in clear (PO question Q-7). Default is pseudonymise.

categories.label: Other organisations named in the document (sub-contractors, banks, guarantors' companies)
categories.keep_list: Public bodies, courts, tribunals, arbitral institutions, regulators and standards bodies (e.g. PDPC, MAS, IMDA, SIAC, SIMC, Supreme Court, ACRA, IRAS, ISO) are KEEP: the legal analysis depends on them. Maintained as `keep_list_public_bodies`.

categories.label: Unique Entity Number (UEN) and foreign company registration numbers
categories.personal_data_note: Business identifier, not personal data; a sole proprietorship UEN can relate to an identifiable individual (treat as personal data then).

detection.notes: UEN formats per ACRA/UEN conventions are to verify (8 digits + letter for ROB businesses; 9 digits starting with year of registration + letter for local companies; T/S/R + 2-digit year + 2-letter entity type + 4 digits + letter for others). UEN check letter algorithm not verified; pattern + context only.

categories.label: Firm file references, matter names, deal code names
categories.personal_data_note: File references often embed client or lawyer initials.

detection.notes: Matter name and code name from the intake record are dictionary matches.

dictionary_examples: Project Example (matter code name from the intake record)

keep_list_public_bodies: Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore
keep_always: Statute names and section references (needed for the Verification Ledger)
Case citations and case names in citations (needed for the Verification Ledger; FR-6.2)
Contract dates other than dates of birth
Governing law, jurisdiction, country and city names
Corporate monetary amounts, fees, caps and percentages (unless personal_financial applies)
Defined terms that are not themselves names
